title: Tradeoffs between objective outcomes and human enjoyment of work in human-AI task allocation
abstract: arXiv:2611.31095v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: For people, tasks at work are defined by more than their outcome: they are colored by the experience of engaging in that task. As AI systems become increasingly capable of performing human-level work they may be deployed to tasks that people find enjoyable while simultaneously creating comparatively more aversive tasks such as monitoring AI outputs. This creates a thorny tradeoff for managers: whether work should be assigned purely based on the expected performance of the workers in question, or also account for the subjective experience of the person potentially doing the task. Most economic accounts focus on expected utility calculations based on the former. Here, we assess how people balance objective outcomes and more subjective qualities like enjoyment. translated_title: 人机任务分配中客观结果与人类工作乐趣之间的权衡
translated_abstract: 对人们而言，工作中的任务不仅仅由其结果来定义：参与任务的过程体验同样为任务赋予了色彩。随着AI系统越来越有能力完成人类水平的工作，它们可能会被部署到人们觉得有趣的任务上，与此同时却创造出相对更令人厌烦的任务，例如监控AI的输出。这给管理者带来了一个棘手的权衡：工作应该纯粹基于相关工作者的预期绩效来分配，还是也应该考虑潜在执行任务者的主观体验。大多数经济学理论聚焦于基于前者的期望效用计算。在本研究中，我们评估了人们如何在客观结果与乐趣等更主观的品质之间进行权衡。在一系列大规模（N=800）行为研究中，人们需要将任务分配给AI或人类工作者，我们发现人们的分配决策最能被一种……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过大规模行为实验（N=800）揭示，人们在对AI与人类工作者进行任务分配时，并非仅基于客观绩效结果，而是会在客观结果与工作乐趣等主观体验之间进行权衡。
en_tdlr: Large-scale behavioral studies (N=800) reveal that when allocating tasks between AI and human workers, people balance objective performance outcomes against subjective factors like the enjoyment of doing the work.
